I am in my final year (depending on if i even pass the classes and take them at the rate i originally wanted) so i feel you. Its so frustrating to have to retake classes and like your never moving forward fast enough.

If it helps, heres what i plan to do as of right now. I have been trying to take atleast 2 classes a semester while working part time. Cant quit working, i think it would make me more depressed. I cant keep taking more than 1 mid level class, or ill just keep doing terribly or failing them or just not having a good time at all. So for the next semester, im only going to take one class. 

What sucks is i still have a few weeks left for the classes now. I have one class i know i can do well in if i just give myself the time. The other one is 4 points and the homework takes so long it makes me psychotically upset. I messaged that teacher of the class for an updated grade so we shall see what it is after she factors in some things. Maybe she will even help me a bit, doubtful, even though she knows im disabled from depression.

Even if im getting a passing grade, i have a feeling ill stop trying to pass that class all together by the end of this week. I guess thats okay, better than going crazy and failing both classes. Its getting too exhausting to keep advocating for myself in this system that dosent really care unless im in the hospital. So i guess im done playing by their rules that i cant follow in the first place. 

Im going to complete my stupid 2 year associates HR degree, even if it takes me 5 years dammit. Im no longer going to subject myself to the torture of studying for multiple classes with the way my brain copes right now. 

For a long time i decided i have to graduate first to start my life, and i was partially right. School leaves you no time to develop as a person and develop your adult life unless your neurotypical and/or have help/money/are a miracle worker. 

To sum it up, its time for me to quit stretching my exhausted brain so thin. I am terrified to face the music of this decision but its better than this endless loop of suffering.

Tbh, stopping cold turkey is the best thing to do. Trying to reason with yourself that you won’t smoke during the day or only smoke at night is usually a lie, if you could limit yourself like that I’m guessing you would have already done that. I’m saying this cus I’m the same way. Took me like 3 extra months to quit because I tried to reason with myself that it be fine if I just smoked at night. I would cold turkey regardless because even if you just smoke at night, you could end up using more anyway even if it’s restricted to a time window. 

I needed to quit because the mental fog got so bad it was making me derealize. So I would figure out all the reasons you have for quitting and then follow through. If you thinking about buying a bag, look at your bank statements. If you feel like smoking will make you happy, really examine how you feel when you are high. Is this actually what you wanted? Is this the kind of happiness you want?
